title: Script attributes and theming
text: The data attributes the embed script reads, and how to make the card match your site. Attributes The card is a web component Light, dark and auto Custom properties Where to load the script The embed is a single script tag. Configuration lives in data- attributes on it. Attributes Attribute Values Default What it does --------------- ---------------------------- ------- -------------------------------------------------------------------- data-key your bk… site key none Required. Identifies your tool. data-ctx an artifact id, e.g. pdf none Default context for every baton.pass() call on the page. data-theme auto, light or dark auto The card's color scheme. auto follows the visitor's system setting. data-position inline or toast inline inline draws the card in the page; toast shows it as a small pop-up card. A ctx passed directly to baton.pass() overrides data-ctx. The card is a web component The card renders as a custom element, , and its markup and styles live in a Shadow DOM. That has two consequences: - Your CSS can't restyle the inside of the card by accident, and the card's CSS can't leak into your page. - The card stays readable on any background, because it brings its own surface, text and focus styles. Light, dark and auto Use data-theme to choose the card's scheme: - auto follows the visitor's system preference (prefers-color-scheme). - light and dark force one scheme, for example when your site has its own theme switch. Custom properties Custom properties inherit through the Shadow DOM boundary, so you can set them on the baton-card element, or on any ancestor, from your normal stylesheet. Three are supported: Property What it controls ---------------- --------------------------------------------------- --baton-accent The accent color: the button and highlights. --baton-radius The card's corner radius. --baton-font The font family used inside the card. Those three are the whole styling surface. There is no way to reach into the card's internals, and that is deliberate: it keeps every card recognisable, legible and accessible, wherever it appears. Custom properties work on every plan. Hiding the "passed by Baton" mark is part of the Anchor plan and above. Where to load the script Put the script in the (or, in a framework, wherever you load third-party scripts) and keep async. It is small, doesn't block rendering, and does nothing until you call pass(). See the framework recipes for React, Next.js, Vue, Svelte and plain HTML.

title: React, Next.js and other frameworks
text: Load the script once, call baton.pass() when the job is done. Recipes for React, Next.js, Vue, Svelte and plain HTML. React Next.js Vue Svelte Plain HTML Testing The recipe is the same everywhere: load the script once, then call window.baton?.pass() when your tool succeeds. Frameworks only change where those two lines live. React Load the script in your index.html, then call pass() from an effect that runs when the job finishes: The declare global block gives window.baton a type. Put it in a .d.ts file if you use it in more than one component. Next.js Load the script once in the root layout with next/script. It passes data- attributes through: Then call pass() from a client component, exactly as in the React recipe: In development, React runs effects twice. That can request two cards. It doesn't happen in production, but if it bothers you, guard the call with a ref. Vue Load the script in your index.html (or with useHead if you use Nuxt). Svelte Using Svelte 5 runes: Add the script tag to app.html in SvelteKit. Plain HTML No build step needed: Testing - In tests, don't load the script. window.baton?.pass() is a no-op when baton is missing. - Use your real site key in staging to see real cards. Impressions and clicks from staging count like any others, so use a separate tool entry if you don't want them mixed with production.

title: baton.pass() reference
text: The JavaScript API. One function, two optional arguments, one boolean back. Options ctx target Return value When to call it Before the script has loaded Under the hood Once the embed script has loaded, it defines window.baton. It has one method. Options Option Type What it does -------- ------------------- ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ ctx string The artifact your tool just produced, such as "pdf" or "transcript". Optional. target Element, selector Where the card should be mounted. Optional; without it the card appears according to data-position. ctx ctx is one of the artifact ids from Picking inputs and outputs. It narrows the match: if your tool lists pdf and image as outputs, passing ctx: "pdf" tells Baton this particular success moment ended with a PDF, so the card is for tools that take one. Without ctx, Baton considers all of your tool's outputs. You can also set a default for the whole page with the data-ctx attribute; a ctx passed to pass() wins. target Pass either a DOM element or a CSS selector: The card is drawn inside a Shadow DOM, so your page's CSS can't break it and it doesn't leak into yours. See theming. Return value pass() returns a promise for a boolean: Resolves to Meaning ----------- ---------------------------------------------------------------------------- true A card was found and shown. false There is no match right now. Nothing was shown, and nothing else happens. false is not an error. It is the normal answer whenever no tool fits the journey, every fitting tool is a competitor or is out of credits, or the visitor has hit a fairness limit. Use it if you want to show something of your own in the same spot: When to call it Call pass() at the success moment, once per success: - After the file has been compressed and the download is available. - After the transcript has rendered. - After the export finished, not while it is running. Avoid calling it on page load, on errors or in a loop. A card is worth showing when the person has just got what they came for. Before the script has loaded The script is loaded with async, so window.baton can be undefined for a moment. Guard with optional chaining: Under the hood pass() asks the public card endpoint for a match using your site key and ctx, and renders the answer. If you would rather build your own card UI, you can call that endpoint yourself.

title: Getting started
text: Add your tool, paste one line, call baton.pass() when it succeeds. About two minutes. 1. Add your tool 2. Paste the script 3. Call baton.pass() at the success moment 4. Check it works What next You need a tool with a clear moment when it has finished its job, and a page where that moment happens. That is all. 1. Add your tool Create an account and add your tool from the dashboard. You will be asked for: - Name and URL: what people will see on other tools' cards. - Category: used to keep competitors apart. Two tools in the same category are never paired unless both opt in. - Inputs: what people bring to your tool (a PDF, a photo, an idea). - Outputs: what people leave with (a compressed PDF, a transcript, a logo). - Card copy: a short title, a line of body text and a button label for the card other tools show about you. Inputs and outputs come from a fixed list. Picking them well is the single biggest factor in whether your card is shown to the right people: read Picking inputs and outputs if you are unsure. Your tool starts with 10 credits, so it can be shown before it has sent anyone anywhere. 2. Paste the script Each tool has a public site key that starts with bk. It identifies your tool and is not a secret. Put this in the of the page where your success moment happens: The script loads asynchronously, so it doesn't block rendering. Nothing appears on the page until you ask for it in the next step. 3. Call baton.pass() at the success moment Call it right after your tool has done its job, not on page load: ctx says which of your outputs this moment produced. If your tool can produce several kinds of result, it narrows the match to the one the person is actually holding. The optional chaining (?.) means nothing breaks if the script is slow to load or blocked by an extension. 4. Check it works Open the page, complete the job your tool does, and watch for the card. A few things to know: - You may see no card at first. Matching only shows tools that fit your outputs, have credits and aren't your competitors. On a young network there are fewer to choose from, and that is normal. baton.pass() resolves to false when there is no match. - Your own tools are never shown to you. Baton skips any tool owned by the same account as the host. - Your dashboard shows the install. The first time the embed renders on your site, your tool is marked as installed. What next - Change where and how the card appears: Script attributes and theming. - Wire it into a component: Framework recipes. - Learn how credits flow: The credit exchange.

title: Introduction
text: What Baton is, how a pass works, and where to find everything in these docs. How a pass works Where to go next Searching Baton is a recommendation network for the success moment: the second a tool finishes its job. A file is compressed, audio is transcribed, a logo is exported. The person is holding a result and wondering what to do with it. That is when your tool calls baton.pass(), and Baton shows one card for the most useful next tool. How a pass works 1. Every tool on the network says what people bring to it (its inputs) and what they leave with (its outputs), using one shared vocabulary of artifacts. 2. When your tool succeeds, it calls baton.pass(). 3. Baton looks for a tool whose inputs match what your tool just produced: a compressed PDF goes to a tool that takes a PDF. That is journey-based matching. 4. One card appears. If the visitor clicks, they arrive on the other tool through a signed link, and credits move one for one: you earn 1, the tool they visited spends 1. If nothing suitable exists, nothing is shown. baton.pass() resolves to false and your page carries on. Where to go next I want to… Read ------------------------------------------- ------------------------------------------------------------- Get a card on my site in two minutes Getting started Look up the JavaScript API baton.pass() Change how the card looks Script attributes and theming Use it from React, Vue, Svelte or plain HTML Framework recipes Describe my tool correctly Picking inputs and outputs Understand credits The credit exchange See what stops abuse Fairness and anti-fraud Know what data is stored Privacy Build against the API REST API Trails are step-by-step routes between free tools for people who just want to get a job done. They are the same idea, written down for humans. Searching Press ⌘ K (or Ctrl K ) anywhere in the docs to search.

title: The credit exchange
text: Credits move one for one. Send a visitor to earn one, receive a visitor and spend one. The rule Starting balance What earns a credit When you run out Reading your balance Plans and credits Baton runs on a simple exchange. Nobody bids for a slot and nobody pays to be shown on a free plan. Attention flows between tools, and credits keep it balanced. The rule What happens Your credits ------------------------------------------------------- ------------ A visitor clicks the card on your site +1 A visitor arrives at your tool from another's card −1 One click sent earns one credit. One visitor received costs one. There is no exchange rate, no multiplier and no hidden fee. Starting balance Every new tool starts with 10 credits, so it can be shown to real people before it has sent anyone anywhere. The first 100 tools on the network keep double starter credits: 20 instead of 10. What earns a credit Only a credited click moves credits. A click still takes the visitor where they wanted to go, but it doesn't count towards credits when it breaks one of the fairness rules: - A second click from the same visitor to the same tool within 24 hours. - A fourth or later credited click from the same visitor on the same host in one day. Credits are settled through signed links that Baton generates for each card, so a click can't be forged for a card that was never shown. When you run out A tool with 0 credits isn't shown on other tools' cards until it sends traffic of its own. That isn't a penalty on your own site. Your embed keeps working, your visitors keep seeing cards for other tools, and every click they make earns you a credit. As soon as you have one, you are eligible to be shown again. Reading your balance Your dashboard shows your current balance and the ledger behind it: a line for the starting credits and one for every click sent or received. The balance is always the sum of the ledger. Plans and credits The exchange works the same on every plan. Plans change what you can do around it: Plan Price Tools Handshakes Stats ------ --------- --------- ---------- ---------------------- Relay Free 1 none 7 days Anchor $12/month 5 up to 25 90 days Studio $39/month Unlimited Unlimited 365 days, plus the API A handshake is a mutual, direct pairing between two tools that both agree to it. Handshakes rank first when Baton chooses a card. See pricing for the full comparison. Credits are earned by sending visitors, never bought. Paid plans buy more tools, handshakes and longer stats, not more credits.

title: Fairness and anti-fraud
text: How Baton chooses a card, who is never paired, and what stops credits from being farmed. How a card is chosen The rules Competitors are never paired Duplicate clicks aren't credited A daily cap per visitor A daily cap per network Anonymous visitors only Earn your place Handshakes are mutual How clicks are protected What we don't do A recommendation network is only worth being on if the recommendations are good and the credits mean something. These are the rules that protect both. How a card is chosen When a host calls baton.pass(), Baton considers tools that are eligible and ranks them. A tool is eligible when it is: - active, and has at least 1 credit; - not the host itself, and not another tool owned by the host's owner; - not blocked by the host, individually or by category; - not a same-category competitor of the host, unless both tools opt in. Eligible tools are ranked by: 1. Journey fit: how well the tool's inputs match what the host just produced. 2. Handshakes: accepted, mutual pairings rank first. 3. Quality: a smoothed click-through rate. New tools start at the network baseline and move up or down as people react to their card, so a strong card earns more exposure and a weak one less. 4. A little rotation: equally good tools take turns, so the same one doesn't win every time. Nothing about the ranking can be bought on the free plan. Handshakes are the only paid element, and they need both tools to agree. The rules Competitors are never paired Two tools in the same category are never paired unless both opt in. Your card won't put a rival's tool in front of your own users by accident. Duplicate clicks aren't credited If the same visitor clicks through to the same tool more than once within 24 hours, only the first click is credited. They still reach the tool. A daily cap per visitor At most 3 credited clicks per visitor, per host, per day. Someone clicking every card a tool shows, over and over, can't be turned into credits. A daily cap per network At most 10 credited clicks per network address, per host, per day, however many browsers it claims to be. Rotating user agents from one machine can't farm credits, and an office or school behind a single address still counts. Anonymous visitors only Visitors are identified only by an anonymous hash that rotates every day, so nobody can be followed from one day to the next. See Privacy. Earn your place A tool with 0 credits isn't shown until it sends traffic. Being on the network means giving as well as receiving. Handshakes are mutual Paid plans can set up handshakes: direct pairings between two tools that both agree to it. They rank first between those two tools. You can't buy a spot on a site whose owner hasn't agreed. How clicks are protected - Signed links. Every card links to a signed /r/ address. The signature covers the impression, the host and the tool shown, and expires after 24 hours. A link can't be forged for an impression that never happened, or redirected to a different tool. - One click per impression. The database allows a single click per impression. - Redirect, then attribution. The link takes the visitor to the tool and adds ?ref=baton so the destination can see where they came from. - Uncredited is not blocked. A click that breaks a rule still works for the visitor. It just doesn't move credits, and it is recorded as uncredited. What we don't do - No pay-to-rank on free plans. - No ads in the slot. - No tracking cookies, and no cross-site profiles. - No fake testimonials, users or statistics anywhere on this site. If you think a tool is gaming the network, tell us and we will look at it.

title: Picking inputs and outputs
text: How to describe your tool with the shared artifact vocabulary, and the full list to choose from. How to choose Categories Artifacts Documents Images Audio & video Words Web & code Data Work Baton matches tools by journey, not by keyword. Every tool declares two lists, both drawn from one shared vocabulary of artifacts: - Inputs: what people bring to your tool. - Outputs: what people leave with. When a tool calls baton.pass(), Baton looks for a tool whose inputs match what the host tool just produced as an output. Someone who has just made a PDF is ready for a tool that takes a PDF. How to choose - Describe the person's hands, not your product. A PDF compressor takes pdf and leaves people with pdf. Its category is documents, but what it produces is what decides who it is shown to. - List what is true most of the time. Two or three honest outputs beat ten hopeful ones. Every extra output widens the match, and a match on something you rarely produce is a poor card. - Be specific when it helps. podcast says more than audio, and transcript more than text. Use the general one when the specific one would be wrong. - Use ctx to say which output this moment produced. If your tool can output a pdf or an image, pass ctx: "pdf" when it made a PDF. - Inputs matter as much as outputs. They decide which tools' hosts will send people your way. Categories Every tool also has one category. Two tools in the same category are competitors and are never paired, unless both opt in. Choose the category that describes what the tool is. Category id ------------------- -------------- Documents & PDF documents Images & design images Audio & podcasts audio Video video Writing writing Developer tools developer Data & spreadsheets data Marketing & social marketing Productivity productivity Websites & no-code web Learning education Something else other Artifacts The full vocabulary, grouped. Use the id in data-ctx and in baton.pass( ). The dashboard shows the same list with the labels. Documents Files people read, sign or send. Artifact id --------------- ------------- PDF pdf Document document Spreadsheet spreadsheet Slide deck slides Signed document signature Résumé resume E-book ebook Images Anything visual, from a screenshot to a brand. Artifact id ------------- -------------- Image image Photo photo Screenshot screenshot Logo logo Icon set icon Illustration illustration Mockup mockup Diagram diagram Color palette palette Font pairing font QR code qr Audio & video Sound and moving pictures, raw or finished. Artifact id ---------------- ------------------ Audio audio Podcast episode podcast Voice recording voice Music track music Video video Short clip clip GIF gif Subtitles subtitles Screen recording screen-recording Words Text in every stage, from idea to translation. Artifact id ---------------- ------------- Plain text text Transcript transcript Article article Notes notes Email email Newsletter issue newsletter Social post social-post Translation translation Summary summary Idea idea Web & code Things that live on the internet or run on a computer. Artifact id ------------ -------------- Website website Landing page landing-page Link link Code code API api App build app Domain domain Form form Data Numbers, tables and what they turn into. Artifact id ---------------- ---------------- Dataset data CSV csv JSON json Chart chart Survey results survey-results Analytics report analytics Work Plans, schedules and the paperwork of getting things done. Artifact id ------------- ----------- Task list task-list Meeting meeting Schedule schedule Invoice invoice Plan plan Portfolio portfolio Audience list audience The list is deliberately small so that matches are meaningful. If your tool's journey doesn't fit, tell us what people bring and what they leave with.

title: Privacy
text: The embed sets no cookies. Visitors are an anonymous hash that changes every day. Here is exactly what is stored. The short version How the visitor hash works What is stored What isn't stored What the tool you pass to sees Web server logs For your own privacy policy Baton exists to pass people on at a good moment, not to follow them. The embed is built so that it can't. The short version - No cookies. The embed doesn't set any, on your site or ours. - No accounts, no profiles. A visitor is never asked who they are. - An anonymous hash, rotated daily. To apply the fairness rules, Baton needs to tell whether two clicks came from the same visitor on the same day. It does that with a hash that changes every day, so the same person can't be recognised the next day. How the visitor hash works When the card is requested, Baton combines the visitor's IP address and browser user agent with the current date and a secret held on the server, and hashes the result. The hash is what is stored. - The raw IP address and user agent are not stored with impressions or clicks. - The date is part of the input, so tomorrow the same visitor produces a different hash. - The hash isn't shown to other tools, and it isn't added to the destination URL. - Clicks also store a second daily hash of the IP address alone, made the same way. It enforces the per-network cap and rotates daily too. What is stored Record What it holds -------------- -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- Impression Which tool asked, which tool was shown, the ctx, the visitor hash and the time. Click The impression it belongs to, the two tools, the visitor and network hashes, whether it was credited and the time. Ledger Credit changes per tool: the starting balance, and one line per credited click. That is the whole list. Nothing about the visitor's identity, browsing history on your site or activity on other sites is collected. What isn't stored - Cookies, or any identifier that survives from one day to the next. - Raw IP addresses or user agents in impression and click records. - Names, email addresses or accounts for visitors. Visitors don't have any on Baton. What the tool you pass to sees A visitor who clicks a card goes through a signed redirect and arrives at the destination with ?ref=baton on the URL. That tells the destination that Baton sent them, and nothing else. Web server logs Like any web service, our hosting provider may keep ordinary request logs, which can include IP addresses, for a limited time to keep the service running and secure. The privacy policy covers this. For your own privacy policy You can describe the embed truthfully as: a script that loads a recommendation card when a task finishes, sets no cookies, and records an anonymous, daily-rotating hash with each impression and click. What your own policy needs to say is for you, and your advisers, to decide.

title: REST API
text: The public card endpoint for building your own card, and the key-authenticated endpoints for your tools and stats. Get a card 200: a card 204: no match Other statuses Clicks Account endpoints Response shape Errors Rate limits There are two kinds of endpoint: - The card endpoint is public. It uses your public site key (bk…) and is what the embed calls. Use it to build your own card. - The account endpoints under /api/v1 are private. They use an API key (sk…) and act as your account. Get a card Parameter Required Description --------- -------- --------------------------------------------------------------------------- key yes The public site key of the host tool, the one where the success moment happens. ctx no The artifact this moment produced, such as pdf. See inputs and outputs. 200: a card The values above are placeholders showing the shape. Field Meaning ---------------- ------------------------------------------------------------------------------- card.title The headline of the card. card.body One line of supporting text. card.cta The button label. card.tool The tool being recommended: its name and the host of its website. card.via Labels of the artifacts that connect the two tools, for example ["PDF"]. card.href A signed /r/ link. Always link to this, never to the tool directly. badge true when the card should show the "passed by Baton" mark (hidden on paid plans). poweredBy Where that attribution points. 204: no match When nothing fits the journey, the endpoint answers 204 No Content with an empty body. Show nothing, or something of your own. This is the same case where baton.pass() resolves to false. Other statuses Status Meaning ------ -------------------------------------------------------------------- 400 The key is missing or malformed. 404 No active tool has that key (unknown, deleted or paused). 429 More than 60 requests a minute from one address. See Retry-After. Clicks card.href is a signed redirect. It checks the signature, applies the fairness rules, moves credits if the click qualifies, then sends the visitor to the tool with ?ref=baton added. Linking anywhere else means the click isn't counted and the credit isn't earned. If you render the card yourself, show the Baton attribution (badge and poweredBy) unless your plan lets you hide it, and don't cache responses for long: a card is chosen for the moment it is requested. Account endpoints These are authenticated with an API key you create at Settings, API keys. The key is shown once when you create it and only its hash is stored, so copy it straight away. Endpoint Scope What it returns ---------------- ------ ----------------------------------------------------------------------- GET /api/v1/tools read The tools on your account, with credits and site keys. Studio plan. GET /api/v1/stats read Credits, passes sent and received, cards shown, and a daily series (?days=, clamped by plan). Studio plan. GET /api/v1/me read The account the key belongs to. Every plan. A key has scopes. read reads your account data and write creates and changes it. A request outside a key's scopes is refused with 403. Response shape Successful responses wrap the result in a data key: Errors Errors are RFC 9457 application/problem+json documents: Status Meaning ------ ---------------------------------------------------- 400 The body isn't valid JSON. 422 The query or body failed validation. 401 No key, or a key that isn't valid. 403 The key lacks the scope, or the endpoint needs Studio. 404 The thing you asked for doesn't exist. 429 You have hit the rate limit. Rate limits Each key gets 60 requests per minute. Responses carry standard RateLimit- headers, and a 429 includes Retry-After with the number of seconds to wait. API keys act as you. Never put one in browser code. The site key (bk…) is the only key that belongs in a page.
